_spec.purpose: Dedupe ledger for carousel topics. The routine MUST read this before topic selection and MUST append the chosen topic after delivery. No topic may repeat within 90 days unless a material new development exists AND the deck is framed as an update (hard fail otherwise).
_spec.matching: Judge semantic similarity, not string equality: compare candidate against topic + angle + entities + keywords of every entry from the last 120 days. Same underlying story reported by a different outlet or with a new URL is STILL a repeat.

entry_schema.headline: the cover line used
entry_schema.outcome_notes: filled by later runs if the human reports performance

entries.topic: Alaska's data center decision month, anchored by the STAK Energy North Slope AI data center lease revolt (ADL 422741)
entries.angle: The 500-plus vs fewer-than-12 public comment revolt on the STAK lease is one of four Alaska AI-infrastructure decisions in July 2026 (Air Force EUL Jun 29, GVEA turbine Jul 13, AKLNG vote Jul 16, STAK comment Jul 17); thesis 'four rooms, one open door' -- only the DNR comment process invites the public.
entities: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
entries.headline: 500 wrote in. Fewer than 12 said yes.

entries.topic: AI drone plus computer-vision salmon counting pilot on the Wood River, tested against Bristol Bay's 70-year human counting towers (2026 sockeye season)
entries.angle: An unproven AI counter still in training is tested against the hand-clicker tower method that has set Bristol Bay escapement since 1955; thesis 'one river, two ways to count it, only one is proven' -- honest about a pilot, and about who counts (partners UW FRI, BBRSDA, BBEDC; ADF&G not directly involved).
entities: Alaska Department of Fish and Game
University of Washington Fisheries Research Institute
entries.headline: One river. Two ways to count it. Only one is proven.

entries.topic: Alaska-built AI volcano monitoring (VOISS-Net seismic deep learning + VolcSARvatory InSAR) watching three simultaneously elevated Alaska volcanoes, scaling to all five USGS observatories
entries.angle: Present-tense vigilance: Great Sitkin erupting (Watch/Orange) with Kupreanof and Shishaldin restless, watched by machine senses built at UAF/AVO (a neural ear + a satellite eye); the blind-mountain tension (Kupreanof has no ground network) and the Alaska-tech-exported-national pride arc.
entries.headline: Three Alaska volcanoes are awake.

entries.topic: Cook Inlet gas STORAGE crisis: RCA denies Enstar's $240M Kenai Loop Pool storage prudency request (Jul 10) as Southcentral's supply ceiling meets AI data-center gigawatt demand
entries.angle: Supply-side ceiling, not decision access. Alaska is asked to power a gigawatt AI boom (STAK 1+GW, some 30% over urban peak) on a gas system that cannot even secure one winter's storage; the RCA rejected the storage fix on July 10 for 'lacking basic information' and Enstar suspended it. Thesis 'store one winter first?' plus The Hold Test (hold the winter, the ground, the bill).
entries.headline: Alaska's gas machine, in cutaway. And the valve that just shut.

entries.topic: Alaska as the world's proving ground for autonomous wildfire-fighting robots: the XPRIZE Wildfire Autonomous Response track finals field-tested via UAF ACUASI on a 1,000 sq km Alaska range
entries.angle: Alaska is the arena, not the backdrop; five finalists (Anduril, Data Blanket, Dryad, FireSwarm Solutions, Wildfire Quest) race to close the detect-decide-dispatch-douse loop with no human, decided September 2026; thesis 'the machines are still auditioning' (a contest winner is not proof), told through a closing Autonomy Ring
entries.headline: First Machine to the Fire

entries.topic: GVEA's July 13 board vote on a second ~$120M LM6000 gas turbine, set against the Air Force AI-data-center land leases and a record fuel-charge spike
entries.angle: Firm power, soft load: a member-owned Interior co-op is asked to finance firm, dated gas capacity now (member debt, ratepayer exposure) while the AI loads that make firm power feel urgent (Air Force EULs at Eielson/Clear/JBER) are still proposals; who pays for the megawatts, decided in executive session. Distinct from No.1's civic-access 'four rooms' frame (this is Interior generation adequacy / who-pays) and from No.4's Cook Inlet gas storage.
entries.headline: The Interior's Power Math ($120 million, one vote today, members own the bill)

entries.topic: ReconCraft (Anchorage, Native-owned SBA 8(a)) won a $24.96M sole-source Navy contract for autonomous low-profile (stealth) vessels, built in Clackamas, Oregon
entries.angle: What 'Alaska' means in the autonomous-defense build-out is, here, a contracting instrument (Native-owned 8(a) status plus an Anchorage address) rather than a shipyard; the boats are welded Outside. Thesis 'the boat is Alaskan, the shipyard is not' via a single waterline that splits Alaska's paper footprint from its physical one.
entries.headline: The boat is Alaskan. The shipyard is not.

entries.topic: NSF Critical Mineral Accelerator Engine in Alaska (UAF-led, announced 2026-07-14): a Regional Innovation Engine funded $15M now and up to $160M over 10 years if milestones met, to use AI to help locate mineral deposits and biological methods to extract them
entries.angle: Honesty-as-edge. Alaska won a real, decade-scale federal bet to find and process critical minerals, but the AI headlining it is a single unbuilt sentence (no model, dataset, or site named) and the $160M is a milestone-gated ceiling; thesis the uncomputed ground / it isn't built yet, the money framed as a ladder not a check, NANA a partner not owner, one illustrative named site.
entries.headline: It isn't built yet.

entries.topic: Quinhagak / Nalaquq Yup'ik drone-piloting and machine-vision training pipeline in the roadless Yukon-Kuskokwim Delta (Native-owned Qanirtuuq subsidiary; a search-and-rescue boat-detection CNN and a polarized-lens salmon counter)
entries.angle: Data-sovereignty of the sensing layer. A village corporation trains its own FAA Part 107 pilots AND owns its own machine vision, so the community owns the machine that watches its own land, waters, and people. Honesty firewall: the training is HUMAN-piloted (never autonomous AI); the only real ML is two Nalaquq prior tools (SAR CNN c14, polarized-lens salmon counting c15) cited as prior published work; thermal reindeer counting and archaeology are human-read, NOT AI. Thesis 'own the eye, don't rent it'. Distinct from No.2 (Wood River AI salmon counting) by subject/place/actor and from No.1 (STAK who-decides) entirely.
entries.headline: No Road Out. Quinhagak Flies Its Own Eyes
entries.sources_lead: KYUK 2026-07-14 (Samantha Watson); Alaska Public Media / Alaska News Nightly 2026-07-14; nalaquq.com; JCMC paper (SAR CNN + salmon counting, background)
entries.outcome_notes: Shipped 9.07 vs 8.3, vector PDF 7.86MB, 9 slides, zero hard fails. 6 scouts + fact-checker + 3 treatments + copywriter + 5 pixel critics (8 ship / 1 revise-then-fixed) + flow (SHIP) + scorer, full studio, no usage-limit degradation. S6 AK3D thermal terrain hero resolved the chronic flat-hero weakness. Runner-up = AIDEA Houston 30-sq-mi free-land data-center giveaway (now tracked on the public docket).

entries.topic: Will an Alaska data center raise your power bill: on-grid vs off-grid and the cost-allocation gap
entries.angle: A myth-correcting ratepayer-economics analysis. Off-grid North Slope (STAK) is behind-the-meter and cannot touch Railbelt bills; the on-grid AIDEA Mat-Su park just advanced by the state can, and there a big load can spread fixed costs and LOWER rates (per a Launch Alaska op-ed) or compete for scarce gas and RAISE them, decided by the rate deal. The gap: Anchorage adopted AO 2026-27 (10 to 2) while the statewide bill HB 259 sits in the House Energy Committee, so no statewide cost-allocation rule exists.
entries.headline: Will a data center raise your power bill?

entries.topic: A physics-informed machine-learning digital twin of one Utqiagvik permafrost road embankment (Penn State), built on two buried 1 km fiber-optic cables and three winters of thermal and seismic data (Sept 2021 to June 2024)
entries.angle: AI that reads Alaska instead of using it. The point is not a smarter guess, it is a forecast the ground itself keeps correcting; the power and the honest limit are the same fact (one lit kilometer). Net-new topic chosen to break a 4-deck data-center run; honesty-forward (single-source attributed, narrow ML not general AI, one prototype not a statewide deployment).
entries.headline: Reading the Frozen Ground at the Top of America
entries.outcome_notes: Score 8.81 (threshold 8.3), no hard fails. Chosen over an in-window STAK data-center re-touch (11 days after No.1, would be the 5th data-center deck) to protect feed variety. Single-source (Phys.org; JGR paywalled/not independently checked) framed honestly on S8 and in the first comment. Story ~5 weeks old, framed as recent research not breaking news.

entries.topic: Alaska schools writing the rules for AI in the classroom, anchored by Kenai Peninsula Borough School District's proposed AI policy
entries.angle: The tools arrived before the rules: KPBSD already spent $8,300 on a MagicSchool subscription while its governing AI policy is still a draft; the two real questions are who defines academic honesty and who guards student data, and the smart move is to write the policy in pencil (revisable) not ink. Framed against Alaska's 2025 DEED K-12 AI framework (32nd state, 7 principles, 6-step process) as labeled context.
entries.headline: AI is already in class. The rulebook is still in pencil.

entries.topic: AI acoustic and satellite monitoring of the endangered Cook Inlet beluga whale (NOAA Fisheries + Microsoft AI for Good + ADF&G dual-stage deep-learning detector-classifier)
entries.angle: A better ear is not a recovery. AI gives Alaska's most endangered whale a sharper always-on ear (and, separately, satellite eyes) that tells managers where and when the Cook Inlet belugas are in a wall of ship noise, but hearing is not healing: the machine measures the whale, it cannot move it. Net-new marine-mammal AI pivot off the fatigued data-center beat; honesty-forward (hedged 331, no invented accuracy figure).
entities: Alaska Department of Fish and Game
entries.headline: Now a machine can hear them through the ship noise.
entries.outcome_notes: Shipped 8.77 vs 8.3, 9 slides, vector PDF 7.8MB, zero hard fails. Full studio (6 scouts + fact-checker + 3 treatment-directors + copywriter + 5 pixel critics + flow-critic + scorer). Net-new marine-mammal acoustic AI, deliberate break from the 4-deck data-center fatigue. Weakest = artwork-craft (7): the S3 beluga shipped as the designed Canvas fallback (akthree transparent-subject snapshot sentinel false-negatived) and reads flat.

entries.topic: Alaska DNR preliminary decision (ADL 234762) to convey about 19,950 acres (~31 sq mi) of public land two miles north of Houston, Mat-Su, to AIDEA at NO cost for a multi-use industrial and energy district that includes scalable data centers; public comment closes 5 p.m. Aug 19, 2026
entries.angle: The giveaway, surveyed. The state is not waiting for AI infrastructure, it is pre-paying for it by handing its own development authority a township-sized block of public land for nothing, betting free ground summons data centers; the giveaway IS the subsidy and the comment window is the last price control. Public-land-and-process framing (who decides, who pays, the Houston ban) - deliberately NOT the power-bill economics of No.10 (07-18) nor the North Slope STAK campus of No.1 (07-08).
entries.headline: 31 square miles of public land. Free.
entries.outcome_notes: Shipped 8.86 vs 8.3, 9 slides, vector PDF 8.82MB, zero hard fails. Full studio (6 scouts + fact-checker + 3 treatment-directors + copywriter + 5 pixel critics + flow-critic + scorer). AI-infrastructure land decision (data centers = AI's physical plant); distinct DECISION/angle/entities from prior data-center decks. Weakest = artwork-craft (7): low-poly terrain coarse under zoom + the S2 raised cadastral plate read flat despite layered drop-shadows.

entries.topic: How Alaska's tribal health system is governing AI and machine learning on its own data under Indigenous data sovereignty, documented in a peer-reviewed International Journal of Circumpolar Health paper (2026-05-23); ANTHC, Southcentral Foundation, Maniilaq, with Stanford and UAF.
entries.angle: Adopt fast, govern first, on the Tribe's own authority. Indigenous data sovereignty (CARE + FAIR) decides what runs on Alaska Native health data. Deployed Cerner AI Scribe kept distinct from a proposed medevac decision-support model. Alaska stakes air-evac at least 40x, over 80% roadless. SINGLE-SOURCE, about nine weeks old, framed as governance context not breaking news (58e honesty). Chosen after the intended pick (XPRIZE wildfire finals) was a dedupe collision with No.5 (2026-07-12).
entities: UAF Center for Alaska Native Health Research
entries.headline: Governed First
entries.outcome_notes: Shipped 8.90 vs 8.3, 9 slides, vector PDF 2.8MB, zero hard fails. Single-source governance-context deck, honestly framed.

entries.topic: The STAK Energy North Slope AI data-center public revolt reaches its decision point. Alaska DNR's preliminary decision (ADL 422741) to lease Stak Energy 715.4 acres near Deadhorse for a gas-fired AI data center drew more than 500 public comments to fewer than a dozen in support; the written comment window CLOSED July 17, 2026 and the 50-year lease now sits with DNR's Division of Oil and Gas for a final finding.
entries.angle: Consent / who holds the pen, shipped as the post-comment-closure UPDATE to No.1 (2026-07-08), which anchored a four-rooms survey on this SAME STAK docket while the comment window was still OPEN. This is a single-story deep-dive at the decision point: the machine at continental scale (1 to 3 GW, about 30% over urban Alaska peak, 350 to 500 MMcf/day gas), the honesty SORT (the loudest fear, higher home power bills, is the weakest because the North Slope campus self-generates off the Railbelt grid; the strongest hold, 50 years of public land, 7.1M cu yd gravel, gas by the day), and the unsigned pen. Material development vs No.1: the comment window CLOSED July 17, now pending final finding, said so on the cover peg.
entries.headline: 500 to Fewer Than 12. One Office Holds the Pen.
entries.sources_lead: Alaska DNR ADL 422741 primary notice + Anchorage Daily News + Northern Journal (Northern Center lease-doc review for hedged figures)
entries.outcome_notes: Scored 8.66 vs 8.3, zero hard fails, vector PDF 3.39MB. SAME-DOCKET REVISIT of No.1 (2026-07-08): missed in Phase 4 because dedupe_check output was read with `tail`, truncating its TOP match (No.1, jaccard 0.279, same ADL, same 500-vs-12 cover). Shipped honestly as an explicit post-comment-closure UPDATE (cover peg COMMENT CLOSED JULY 17) and flagged for the maintainer. Craft: S3 akthree rendered tundra-machine + S7 akrelief material chips broke the recurring flat-hero ceiling (scorer called them the strongest artwork the series has shipped); artwork-craft still capped 7 for dead lower zones (S2/S5/S8/S9).

entries.topic: AI-industry money becomes a measurable presence in Alaska's 2026 governor race. Campaign finance reports made public the week of July 20 show Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins with the field's largest reported haul, 1.8 million dollars, most of it from Lower 48 donors per ADN, including 372,000 dollars from six employees of the AI company Anthropic and a 100,000 dollar largest single gift from an employee who grew up in Soldotna and now lives in Berkeley.
entries.angle: The asymmetry of the public record, NOT corruption. Disclosure of campaign money is compulsory and disclosure of AI policy is voluntary, so Alaska knows to the dollar who paid for this race and almost nothing about what any of the 17 candidates would do with AI. Thesis 'on file, off record'. Fairness is architectural rather than a footnote: slide 04 disarms the deck's own accusation at the same depth and the same scale, carrying Heilala's 1.4 million dollars of his own money (more than all six Anthropic employees gave) and the candidate's own line that his national donors' only agenda is whether he can win. No causation asserted anywhere, no donor motive on record, no wrongdoing alleged. First elections, campaign-finance and candidate-platform deck of the series.
entries.title: On File, Off Record. Alaska's AI Governor Race.
entries.dedupe_note: dedupe_check.py exit 0, no LIKELY DUPLICATE. Strongest match No.14 (2026-07-22) at token_jaccard 0.022 with ZERO shared entities; the only shared keyword was 'center' from the candidate keyword 'data center moratorium'. Full output read, never tailed. Nothing in the 120-day window touches elections, campaign money, candidates or candidate AI platforms.
entries.conflict_of_interest: The deck concerns donations by six Anthropic employees and was produced by a routine running on a Claude model built by Anthropic. Disclosed on slide 09 at full headline scale, in a pointer chip on slide 02, in the caption, and at the top of the first comment.

entries.topic: Gov. Dunleavy signed the White House Ratepayer Protection Pledge governors addendum (2026-07-23), a voluntary and non binding commitment that AI data center load pays for its own power, and the only Alaska utility on the 281 name signatory list is Cordova Electric Cooperative
entries.angle: A promise is not an instrument. The deck's subject is ENFORCEABILITY, not rate economics. Three instruments are ranked by holding strength (a pledge that binds nobody, a statute that died in House Community and Regional Affairs, and the commission approved contract SB 250 would have created and never did), and Alaska holds only the weakest. The one Alaska signature came from a 1,566 customer cooperative with 18 MW of generation that is not connected by transmission line to any other community and already hosts a 150 kW data center on hydro.
entries.headline: One Alaska utility signed. Its wires reach no one else.
entries.outcome_notes: Adjacent to No.10 (07-18) on the cost allocation gap; dedupe_check returned SOFT OVERLAP ONLY at jaccard 0.096. Deliberately does NOT re-litigate on grid vs off grid economics, and keeps STAK and the Mat-Su parcel in the docket rather than the deck.

entries.topic: Shinkei Systems puts its PSDN-S computer-vision harvesting robot on Cook Inlet salmon boats during the 2026 sockeye season, automating the Japanese ike jime technique in 6.5 seconds or less per fish
entries.angle: The machine does not make a better fish, it manufactures TIME (about 7 hours of rigor becomes up to 60 by the company's own figure), and every asset built out of those hours is held outside Alaska (the Seremoni Grade brand, a 16,000 sq ft Tacoma plant, the NERA freshness dataset, an El Segundo HQ). Deliberately NOT a grievance: the machines go on the boats free and the company splits proceeds variably with fishermen, which the deck states at full weight on slide 06. Thesis 'somebody else owns the clock'. Also an evidence deck, since every performance number in the story is a vendor number and slide 04 says so.
entities: Alaska Department of Fish and Game
entries.headline: Not a better fish. More hours.

entries.topic: Alaska appears exactly once on the Department of Energy's Genesis Mission award list, posted 2026-07-22, and its one row is AURORA-AI, a University of Alaska Fairbanks project led by Richard Wies whose subject is Alaska's own utility resilience
entries.angle: The inversion. Every Alaska AI story this month has been about AI arriving to TAKE power; the one federal AI award that actually landed here points the other way, at the grid, and it posted six days before Southcentral utility executives warned of likely rolling blackouts. Honesty-forward, because nobody has published what the project does or what it is worth, and the deck says so on three slides.
entities: Alaska Center for Energy and Power
entries.headline: 278 federal AI projects. Alaska has one.
entries.outcome_notes: Score 8.09 against a relaxed 7.7 threshold after 4 revision rounds, 0 hard fails. Chosen over the gas-curtailment story, which was the day's strongest news peg but failed the dedupe gate with five LIKELY DUPLICATES, and over the RTO closed-rooms story, which lost its spine at fact-check when akleg.gov 403'd on SB 250 and no source connected the Railbelt tariff to large new loads. Runner-up GAIA (NSF 2608510) is fully verified in this run's claims and available to a later run.

entries.topic: Alaska's individual campaign contribution limit is printed as $500 in AS 15.13.070(b) as codified and as Unlimited in the Alaska Public Offices Commission's own limits table dated 2026-07-29, because the Ninth Circuit struck the cap on 2021-07-30 and nothing replaced it. Ballot Measure 1, on the same 2026-08-18 primary ballot as the governor's race, asks whether to write $2,000 back in.
entries.angle: THE RULEBOOK, not the donors. Shipped as an EXPLICIT UPDATE to No.17 (2026-07-25), stated on the cover. No.17 was a deck about a RECORD (the money is on file, the motive is not); this is a deck about a RULE, and the decider is the reader with a deadline. The material new development is threefold: the largest donor published his motive on 2026-07-29, ADN reported on 2026-07-30 that Ballot Measure 1 cites these same contributions as its example, and this run verified from primary documents that the statute and the enforcer disagree, that a passed initiative takes effect ninety days after certification and so can't govern the race it shares a ballot with, and that Alaskans wrote the $500 cap themselves in 2006 with 73.00 percent on an August primary ballot. Fairness architectural, four donation totals at one scale with the two floors drawn as open terminals. No causation, no wrongdoing, no advocacy eighteen days before the primary.
entries.headline: $500 in the statute. Unlimited in the table. Same law.
entries.title: Struck. And Still Printed. Alaska's $500 Cap
entries.dedupe_note: dedupe_check.py exit 1 as the queued brief predicted. One LIKELY DUPLICATE, No.17 six days prior, token_jaccard 0.161, 8 shared entities. Full output read, never tailed; the No.17 entry read in full before the directors room. Shipped as an explicit UPDATE on the cover chip and in the caption.
entries.conflict_of_interest: Deck concerns donations by six Anthropic employees and was produced by a routine running on a Claude model built by Anthropic. Disclosed on slide 09 at full headline scale (about 100 px), on the cover chip, in the caption, and at the top of the first comment. This run additionally discloses on the cover that it is the SECOND deck this page has published on these donors in seven days.

entries.topic: Alaska's Division of Elections asked the DMV to compare two lists in March 2026; about 3,500 letters went out and 3,048 registrations were moved to inactive status, weeks before the August 18 primary, on data the elections director called probably very old
entries.angle: NOT AI, AND THAT IS THE POINT. The simplest automated operation in computing, a comparison of two lists, changed 3,048 people's registration status and left the burden of proving it wrong with the person. Before Alaska decides how much authority to hand AI systems, this is the verification bar it applies now. Honesty firewall is the spine, not a caveat: the deck never says the action was illegal (legislators' allegation, tagged on slide), never says no human reviewed (no published account describes a check either way), never claims a name change caused a flag, and prints no ratio across three different counts.
entries.headline: Where Are the 3,048? The Map Alaska Hasn't Drawn
entries.outcome_notes: Scored 7.92 against the relaxed 7.7 threshold (4+ revision rounds). Zero hard fails.

entries.topic: Three Alaska procurement artifacts closing this month buy machine-adjacent work without printing a technology term in their public notices. RFP 2026-0200-0064 (statewide speech-to-text, posted 31 Jul, closes 24 Aug 9:30 A.M.), DMV RFI 02-101-27 (automated compliance, posted 30 Jul, closes 20 Aug), and the Eielson Enhanced Use Lease AFCEC-26-R-0009 (3,967 acres, closes 10 Aug), set against Administrative Order 360, which prints artificial intelligence plainly and routes its own plans to the same public notice system.
entries.angle: The notice is the trigger. A public notice is the only part of a procurement most Alaskans ever see, so its vocabulary decides who knows to look. Scoped strictly to the PUBLIC NOTICE TEXT throughout, never to the solicitation packages, which were not read, and the deck never asserts a machine will do the work.
entities: Office of Procurement and Property Management
entries.headline: One state contract. Every court, borough and tribe may use it.
entries.outcome_notes: Score 8.37 against the relaxed 7.7 threshold after 4+ revision rounds, 0 hard fails. Weakest criterion artwork craft at 6.0, which WAS the declared target. Chosen over the Southcentral power ledger, which was the window's biggest news and failed dedupe with 2 likely duplicates, because No.4 ran that exact supply-ceiling spine 22 days earlier and No.20's own notes record a gas-curtailment story rejected on dedupe three days before this run. Eight of 22 prior decks were in that lane.

entries.topic: Graphite One's proposed Graphite Creek open pit on the Seward Peninsula, the Brevig Mission joint session of 2026-07-28 that opposed it, and the company's own release naming artificial intelligence infrastructure among the end markets for natural graphite
entries.angle: The AI in this story does its work in a SENTENCE before it does any in a supply chain. C01 names AI infrastructure among five end markets for natural graphite AS A CLASS, with no customer, no offtake and no volume, while the same release says the product is aimed primarily at EV batteries and grid storage. Meanwhile the clocks don't match: an executive order on 20 July, a company release two days later, a village of about 400 answering eight days after that, and the Army Corps adding at least a year. Thesis, the other half of the AI build-out's bill comes due on ground somebody lives next to, and neither speed nor delay is automatically right.
entries.headline: A clause mentions AI. The pit is 1.1 miles wide.
entries.outcome_notes: Scored 6.9 (capped by one hard fail; raw 7.67 vs 7.7). Repaired and not re-scored.

entries.topic: FERC opened a public comment window (Federal Register 2026-08-03, docket P-8221-124) on the Alaska Energy Authority's application to amend the Bradley Lake Hydroelectric Project licence, diverting Dixon Glacier meltwater and surface runoff into Bradley Lake, raising the pool about 16 feet, and installing a 0.3 MW micro-hydro turbine in a fishwater release valve
entries.angle: THE ASYMMETRY OF UNITS. One side of Alaska's power ledger is measured to the tenth of a megawatt and the other in acres, and nobody has published the number that would connect them. Supply is documented down to a fishwater release valve, about $400 million and six years for a capacity move of 0.3 MW against a projected 38 percent energy gain. Demand, the Air Force's roughly 4,700 acres across twelve parcels at JBER, Eielson and Clear, is documented in LAND and names no megawatts anywhere in its own release. HONESTY FIREWALL ARCHITECTURAL, nothing in any verified document links the diversion to data centres and slide 09 says so at full weight in the deck's only 500-weight display setting. The deck's original comparison anchor, a reported 100 MW per-project minimum, was KILLED by the fact-checker as a single partisan source and the thesis was rebuilt around the absence instead.
entities: U.S. Department of the Air Force
entries.headline: Drawn to Scale, Except the Demand
entries.outcome_notes: Degraded run. Phase 8 pixel critics and the flow critic were not spawned; context budget was exhausted by the art build. Disclosed in the email and to the scorer.

entries.topic: The Administration for Native Americans published its final Fiscal Year 2026 program policies on 2026-07-28 at 91 FR 47241, standing up three funding opportunities (EAGLE, the AI3 Action Institute, NCNTTA) and leaving SEDS-AK, the Alaska-specific economic development program, out of the set. Two days later it posted the AI3 Action Institute, a single national award with a $3,500,000 ceiling to build an artificial intelligence resource centre for Native communities, with Alaska Native villages under ANCSA named eligible. Both windows close 2026-08-27.
entries.angle: The objection is printed inside the agency's own answer to comments, and so is the reply. The deck refuses the word cancelled, because ANA says SEDS evolved and Tribal Business News says the grants replace it and the record does not settle it. What the record DOES settle is narrower and harder, that the five project areas are now named in the notice where trade press says tribes used to propose their own, so the provable change is who specifies the work rather than a dollar loss. What SEDS-AK was worth is not obtainable and the deck says so on its own slide.
entries.title: Both sides are printed on page 47241

entries.topic: Two Alaska landholders have ground on the market for AI data centers and each one, in its own document, lists the power as something the site does not have. The Air Force offered about 4,700 acres across 12 parcels at JBER, Eielson and Clear and its own solicitation calls the JBER sites insufficient in power; AIDEA's deputy director, defending approximately 19,950 acres north of Houston, printed seven things the project does not yet have with a power source fourth; and Enstar has already turned away new large-scale customers.
entries.angle: THE LAND IS ON OFFER. THE POWER IS NOT. Every load-bearing claim comes from the SELLING side rather than from a critic, so nobody in the deck is contradicted because nobody disagrees. Distinct from No.4 (one RCA storage ruling), No.10 (who pays, cost allocation) and No.14 (the land giveaway itself). Asserts no causation, no coordination, no prediction of failure and no winter adequacy verdict. The original framing, a marketed 4 to 5 cents per kWh against 14 to 17 cents, was KILLED by the fact-checker as unsourced and the reframe is stronger.
entries.headline: The Land Is On Offer. The Power Is Not.
entries.sources_lead: Anchorage Daily News opinion by AIDEA deputy director Brandon Brefczynski, 2026-08-04 (primary) + Alaska Public Media and Alaska Beacon, 2026-07-28
entries.outcome_notes: Shipped 7.93 vs 8.3, below threshold, disclosed. 9 slides, vector PDF 10.76MB. Zero hard fails. qa.py WARN with zero FAILs, bespoke_check WARN at median 0.377 and 61 percent drawn share, aggregate_check PASS with all 14 aggregates declared. DEGRADED: no pixel critics, no flow critic, no copywriter and no scorer subagent were spawned.

entries.topic: Alaska's elections director wrote to lawmakers on August 6th that more than 600 of the roughly 3,000 people moved off the active voter list over a citizenship flag have since been confirmed citizens, that more than 100 said they are not and asked to be cancelled, that about 350 notices came back undeliverable, and that she will not restore anyone unilaterally. The DMV comparison that produced the flags is paused. About 1,900 of the affected registrations produced no reply at all.
entries.angle: AN EXPLICIT UPDATE TO No.22 with a DELIBERATELY DIFFERENT THESIS. No.22 argued about the verification bar. This deck argues about what happens when the burden lands on the person and the person does not answer, so the subject is the 1,900 who are silent rather than the 600 who were found. Every number is set against the population it actually describes, and the deck refuses the one inference a reader wants: it never says how the 600 were identified, because C01 states plainly that 600 is NOT the count who contacted the Division. Publishes no shortfall verdict, no fraud claim and no prediction about the August 18th primary.

entries.outcome_notes: Shipped 8.55 vs threshold 8.0 (and clears the unrelaxed 8.3) after THREE art revision rounds. Cycle 1 scored 6.9, capped by two hard fails, both the same defect family: type laid over lit art with no reserve. 9 slides. entries.topic: The Sitka Tribe of Alaska runs an AI video escapement counter at the Redoubt Lake weir, 15 miles by boat from Sitka. The count sets the subsistence harvest limit, now 100 sockeye a year per household, up from 50. A U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service Tribal Wildlife Grant titled 'Artificial Intelligence for Subsistence Salmon Monitoring and Management' paid $200,000 to INSTALL the system in fiscal 2024, and the Tribe's resource protection director says there is no funding for the weir now, because every grant source they found deals with systems needing remediation.
entries.angle: THE SHAPE OF THE MONEY, not the accuracy and not the ownership. A working instrument is disqualified from funding BY working. Deliberately not No.2's thesis (validation, whether the machine can be trusted against a human baseline) and deliberately not No.9's (ownership of the sensing layer), because the Sitka Tribe is RENTING the eye from a British Columbia project, which makes No.9's thesis factually wrong here as well as repetitive. The deck refuses the accuracy argument entirely and strikes the vendor's published metric so the two incommensurable figures can never meet.
entities: Alaska Department of Fish and Game

Cycle 1 scored 8.14 on the criteria and was capped to 6.90 by two hard fails the machine gates rated as warns: 229,000 rendered white-on-white inside its own bar on slide 07, and six bare non-ordinal dates in the first-comment source block. Both repaired. THE RENDERED LADDER WAS REACHED for the first time in six decks, aksdf chosen because it has no GL context to fall back from.

entries.topic: Kenai Peninsula Borough School District's Policy Review Committee took up AR 6161.5, a NEW technology regulation capping routine instructional technology at 15 minutes a day in kindergarten rising to 90 in fourth and fifth grade and stating that routine daily limits are not established for secondary schools, on the same August 3, 2026 agenda as AR 5131.9 Academic Honesty, the AI regulation, which was posted in two competing drafts and appears to draw no grade line at all
entries.angle: EXPLICIT UPDATE to No.12 (2026-07-20) with a DELIBERATELY DIFFERENT THESIS. No.12 argued ORDER, that the tool arrived before the rule, and used the $8,300 MagicSchool purchase as its spine. This deck argues PRECISION, that one document measures a five year old to the minute and can only describe a seventeen year old with an adjective while the AI regulation beside it draws no grade line. The material new development is AR 6161.5 and BP 6161.5, which came to committee as NEW BUSINESS on August 3rd and did not exist on the public record in July. The $8,300 is demoted to one attributed line. Honesty-forward, because the minute caps are a TECHNOLOGY rule that never mentions AI and the deck prints that as a guard chip on slide 02, and because no minutes are posted for either August 3rd meeting so the deck never says what was decided.
entries.headline: A five year old gets a number. A senior gets an adjective.
entries.outcome_notes: Dedupe was re-run at Phase 6 after a caption director spotted the collision; the Phase 4 run had used a discarded candidate's fingerprint. Shipped with pixel-critic and flow-critic rounds cut at the maintainer's instruction to finish fast.

entries.topic: University of Alaska Fairbanks published the amount and the mechanism behind AURORA-AI on August 11, 2026: $725,000, Richard Wies as principal investigator, with Alaska Center for Energy and Power, Colorado State, the National Laboratory of the Rockies and Cordova Electric Cooperative, combining utility data, virtual replicas of the power grid and AI to forecast demand and detect abnormal operating conditions. The Department of Energy's July 22 Genesis Mission list named the project and printed no amount, and exactly one of its 278 rows is an Alaska institution.
entries.angle: EXPLICIT UPDATE to No.20 (2026-07-30), which shipped the blank. No.20 could only report that a project had been selected; this deck reports what the money is FOR, and its thesis is that the software is not the data centre. Read through Cordova rather than through the award: no transmission line leaves the town, Koplin estimates a fifth to a quarter of its hydropower goes unused every year, and 170 kilowatts of computing already sits twenty feet from the generators at Humpback Creek. Also an explicit CORRECTION to No.18, which recorded 150 kW at Humpback Creek; no page fetched this run carries that figure and every string here reads 170 kW sourced to the National Laboratory of the Rockies, March 5, 2026.
entries.dedupe: Ran twice. No.20 at 13 days, jaccard 0.168, shares AURORA-AI, Wies, UAF, ACEP and DOE, cleared as an update because the amount and the mechanism are the material new development and the update is stated ON the frame in the August 11 rail, not only in the record. No.18 at 17 days, jaccard 0.052, shares Cordova and Greensparc only. The run's strongest new fact, the ENSTAR and HEX emergency arbitration, was REJECTED: the correction under it had already shipped twice inside 30 days and a gas contract with no AI content is a national story with an Alaska sticker.

entries.title: The Anchorage Paper That Wrote Itself, Then Stopped
entries.topic: A synthetic local news site branded "Local News, Anchorage. Every Day." published more than 500 articles between July 8th and July 26th, 2026, carried a notice on every article checked saying no journalist had reviewed it, then stopped publishing and left every page live and indexed.
entries.angle: Full disclosure changed nothing. The site told the truth about being AI written and unreviewed, and the pages still stand up as Anchorage local news, which makes labeling the wrong test and continuity the right one.

entries.title: The Equal-Award Projection, 552 to 1
entries.topic: NSF opened the State and Regional AI Infrastructure Hubs program (solicitation NSF 26-513, posted July 31, 2026, announced August 4, 2026) and wrote into it a rule capping every state at one award. NSF announced it as a $100 million initiative while the solicitation puts anticipated funding at $40 million to $100 million, anticipates 10 awards per cycle against 50 states, and expects proposals to request $4 million to $12 million over 5 years. Full proposals are due November 4, 2026, 82 days from the run date, and deadlines recur on the first Wednesday in November.
entries.angle: THE DENOMINATOR. NSF's own stated problem is that access to AI infrastructure is highly uneven across the nation, and its remedy is distributed at a flat rate, one award per unit, where the unit is the state. A state is a shape with an area and the rule pays no attention to area, so Alaska's 570,641 square miles and Rhode Island's 1,034 carry an identical ceiling that was set before any proposal was read. Deliberately FAIR to NSF, because geographic spread is a defensible reason to cap per state, and the argument survives conceding it. The deck also refuses three things the record does not support, that NSF is spending $100 million flat, that Alaska has applied or been refused, and that a missed cycle is exclusion. Distinct from No. 20 (2026-07-30), which was retrospective about a published DOE award list where Alaska appeared once; this is prospective and about the design of an allocation nobody has answered yet.
entities: State and Regional AI Infrastructure Hubs

entries.title: A Plan, a Study, and No Published Due Date
entries.topic: S. 5171, the Children's AI Toy Safety Act of 2026, taken up by the Senate Commerce Committee at 10:00 a.m. on August 5th, 2026 in room SR-253 on an agenda of five bills, three of which carry AI or a chatbot in the title. Duckworth's office says the bill cleared committee that day with Alaska's Lisa Murkowski as the Republican cosponsor. The release describes an FTC and CPSC coordinated plan and a National Academies study; it names no rule, no ban and no standard. The committee's own meeting page publishes the agenda with every result row blank and no tally for any of the five bills. The bill text returned 403 on August 15th, so no statutory deadline for the plan or the study could be read.
entries.angle: THE MISSING DUE DATE. The deck asks one narrow question the record can actually answer: when is either deliverable owed? Every slide carries an empty DUE field, and it stays empty to the last slide because no published source states a date. The thesis was REBUILT at the claims gate after the fact-checker killed 'Alaska's statute book is empty' as an unverifiable absence; what survived is the narrower, fully sourced claim that the first federal answer to machines that talk to children is a plan and a study whose timing is not on the record. Deliberately fair: a plan and a study is the normal first move on something nobody has measured, and the deck says so in the caption's close. The deck REFUSES to say that Alaska law does not cover AI toys, that the 403 proves anything about the bill's contents, that the committee vote failed, or that any count of AI toys exists behind the senator's word 'thousands'.
entities: Children's AI Toy Safety Act of 2026

entries.title: The Menu and the First Friday
entries.topic: Alaska's Rural Health Transformation Program, first Friday of awards on August 7th, 2026: $4,500,000 moved across nineteen projects out of a $272,174,856 first-year allocation, against the state's own program page listing drones, kiosks and AI-enabled tools as eligible uses
entries.angle: A menu and an order are two different documents. The state wrote what the money MAY buy; the first order bought X-ray machines, a hydroponic farm and a scheduling system. Fourteen of nineteen awards are not itemised in published reporting and the deck says so at full weight.
entries.note: The briefed headline, that the fund bought no autonomy, was killed by the fact-checker: the state publishes the nineteen-project list only as an unparseable spreadsheet. The Alaska Native Language Center candidate was killed outright as a manufactured AI link.

entries.title: The Proving Sky
entries.topic: Alaska Airlines was the first airline to adopt Air Space Intelligence's Flyways machine learning route-optimization tool in 2021, and that Alaska deployment became the demonstration case behind the FAA's $875 million contract with the same company to build SMART, a predictive national airspace system, plus the FMDS flow platform.
entries.angle: The inversion. For a month this page showed Alaska as a site AI is done TO (data centers sited, land leased, power drawn). This deck flips it: Alaska's terrain and weather PROVED the tool the whole country is now buying. Direction of causation runs Alaska to nation.
entries.note: Aviation AI, a fresh uncovered beat. AURORA-AI (No.20, No.31) and the Cook Inlet gas story (adjacent to No.27) were rejected as duplicates at dedupe. Score 8.33 over 8.3.

entries.title: A Poll Is Not a Ballot
entries.topic: A Data for Progress survey published August 17th found 73 percent of Alaska likely voters, including 63 percent of Republicans, support pausing new data center development until the state passes a law regulating it. Nine days earlier the Houston city council in the Mat-Su voted an in-city data center ban down 4 to 2 and unanimously passed two resolutions objecting to the state's land transfer process instead. Anchorage adopted a permitting framework in March. No Alaska election deepfake law is enacted.
entries.angle: The instrument gap. A poll measures a preference and a vote allocates a power, and the deck refuses both cheap readings: not voters betrayed by their council, and not the poll is meaningless. The 73 percent is real and cross-party; the ordinance the council was actually holding reached a small section of one parcel. What Alaska has is a preference with no instrument attached to it.
entries.note: Score 8.07. Dedupe returned 2 likely matches at fingerprint level; the semantic call was NOT a duplicate, with a binding build constraint that the deck must not re-tell No.14's AIDEA parcel conveyance. The fact-check killed the original thesis half (no pause anywhere in Alaska) as an unbounded negative and supplied the Public Citizen tracker replacement.

entries.title: Alaska Bought American. The Tariff Found a Seam.
entries.topic: Proclamation 11055, signed August 13th, 2026 and published August 19th at 91 FR 53699, imposes a 100 percent ad valorem duty on imported uncrewed aircraft over 25 kilograms, on imported aircraft carrying thermal imagers and on imported docking stations, effective 12:01 a.m. eastern September 3rd, 2026, with 25 percent on aircraft of 25 kilograms or less. The duty attaches to goods ENTERED FOR CONSUMPTION, so it is triggered by an import event and not by where a machine was built. Alaska's $12.4 million SOAR initiative bought drones, docking stations and Starlink for communities off the road system, and its phase one aircraft were Skydio X10s that Skydio says are assembled in the United States, so September 3rd does not reach them. The exposure is the second tranche: 25 percent on the Annex III components list, effective February 9th, 2027, which is also 180 days from signing.
entries.angle: A federal trade instrument priced an Alaska search tool without ever naming Alaska. The deck reads the proclamation for what it says rather than for what it was aimed at: the word Alaska appears zero times, search and rescue appears once at the end of a list of federal uses, and the date that reaches Alaska's fleet is not the one in the headlines.
entries.note: Scored 8.39 at revision round 4 after 7.62, 7.99 and a round-3 result of 8.39 capped to 6.9 by one overlap. NOT a repeat of any drone or trade topic in the ledger; the nearest drone entry is No.2, 42 days back and a salmon-counting story.
